Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Money, work & business

tax noun

also taxes, taxation, pay taxes, tax-free, taxpayer, tax collector, impose a tax, income tax, collect taxes

classical

Cic. Man. 17: vectīgālia nervōs esse reī pūblicae
Traupman 169, 180, 390: tax

vectīgal, vectīgālis n.

noun, third declension

a tax; public revenue

Lewis & Short: a toll, tax, impost paid to the State. To impose a tax is vectīgal impōnere (with the dative), to collect taxes vectīgālia exigere, to pay them vectīgālia pēnsitāre (Cic. Man. 16; Traupman 390); a tax collector is exāctor (Traupman 169, 390). Tax-free is vectīgālium immūnis (M-O).

Other words

  • tribūtum, tribūtī n. — a direct tax, a levy; tribute

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.14.1: neque tribūta ūnā cum reliquīs pendunt; Cic. Fam. 3.7.3: intolerābilia tribūta (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: a stated payment, a contribution, tribute: the levy on Roman citizens and the tribute of subject peoples. For customs duties see customs duty.

Examples

  • vectīgālia nervōs esse reī pūblicae semper dūximus

    we have always held taxes to be the sinews of the stateCic. Man. 17

  • Druidēs ā bellō abesse cōnsuērunt neque tribūta ūnā cum reliquīs pendunt

    The druids usually stay out of war, and they do not pay taxes like everyone elseCaes. BG 6.14.1

  • Plērīque, cum aut aere aliēnō aut magnitūdine tribūtōrum aut injūriā potentiōrum premuntur, sēsē in servitūtem dicant nōbilibus

    Most of them, when they are weighed down by debt, by heavy taxes or by the wrongs of the powerful, give themselves up as slaves to the noblesCaes. BG 6.13.2

  • vectīgālia exigere

    to collect taxesTraupman 169

  • vectīgal impōnere

    to impose a taxTraupman 180

  • vectīgal impōnere (+ dat.)

    to impose a tax onTraupman 390

  • vectīgālia pēnsitāre

    to pay taxesTraupman 390

See also customs duty, money, pay, state.
